idScheme.parts: <kind>.<form>[.<sense>]: pre. (prefix), suf. (suffix), root. (root or combining form). A sense tag separates parts spelled the same (pre.un = not, pre.un.rev = undo). A part with variantOf is a spelling variant of that part (pre.im is pre.in before b, m, p).
idScheme.base: base:<word> in a derivation names a free base word that is not listed as a part (base:kind).
idScheme.surface: A derivation may carry surface: the pieces exactly as they are spelled in the word. When surface differs from the parts' own forms, spell says why. surface pieces always join to make the word.
idScheme.transparent: false when the parts help but do not give the meaning of the whole word (permit, understand).
idScheme.grades: Grades where the Word Study Lab offers the part. taughtIn lists the unit ids whose morphFocus names it; other placements are the lab's own.
idScheme.origin: origin_certain is true only when the language of origin is well documented; no origin is guessed.
idScheme.families: words lists every derivation that contains an anchor part (or base: word).

inflections.rule: Add -s to most nouns to mean more than one.
Add -es to nouns that end in s, x, z, ch or sh, so you can hear the extra syllable.
When a noun ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i and add -es.
When a noun ends in a vowel and y, just add -s.
Some nouns that end in f or fe change to v and add -es.
A few common nouns change inside instead of adding an ending. You learn them one at a time.
Add -ed to most verbs to tell about the past.
When a verb ends in silent e, drop the e and add -ed.
When a short verb ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant and add -ed.
When a verb ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i and add -ed.
Add -ing to most verbs to tell what is happening now.
When a verb ends in silent e, drop the e and add -ing.
When a short verb ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant and add -ing.
Add -er to compare two things and -est to compare three or more.
When an adjective already ends in e, add only -r or -st.
When a short adjective ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant first.
When an adjective ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i first.

falseFriends.truth: Butter is one whole word. It is not butt with the doer ending -er.
Corner is one whole word for the place where two edges meet. It is not corn plus -er.
Hammer is one whole word. Ham and mer are not word parts here.
There is no word sist for -er to be added to. Sister is one whole word.
Numb plus -er would mean more numb. The noun number is a different, whole word.
Wat is not a word, so there is nothing for -er to join. Water is one whole word.
Paper is one whole word. Pap and -er are not word parts here.

falseFriends.tempting: a car that is a pet
falseFriends.truth: Carpet is not a compound of car and pet. It is one whole word.
Cattle has nothing to do with cats. It is one whole word.
Hamburger is named after the city of Hamburg. There is no ham in the name.
Sil is not a word, so -ly is not a suffix here. Silly is one whole word.
Belly is one whole word. The ly is not the suffix -ly.
King is one whole word. The ing is not the ending -ing.
Ring is one whole word. The ing is not the ending -ing.
Uncle is one whole word. The un is not the prefix un- here.
Real is one whole word. The re is not the prefix re- here.
Reason is one whole word. The re is not the prefix re- here.
Here port is a word for a harbor or gate, not the root port that means carry.
The vid in divide is not the root vis/vid that means see.
